# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ✋ 👍 👌 ✋ 👎 👎 ✋ 👌 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 👍]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

The previous gesture code was not reliable, so I will now state the bomb facts plainly to the Mute. The display is 0, the light is yellow, the button is large and labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and the wires are blue, yellow, red. The Mute should consult the manual and give the Blind the exact safe procedure; the Blind’s wave likely indicates acknowledgement, not an action instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb facts: display 0; light yellow; large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 red. Read the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Wait for Mute's manual-based instructions. Do not act on the button or wires yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋ 👍]

The Mute has signalled, but the gestures do not establish a safe operation for the Blind. The bomb state is unchanged, and I should not invent a meaning for the signs or cause an action without the manual-based instruction reaching the Blind.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

The Mute still has not conveyed a manual-derived instruction to the Blind. I will explicitly request that the Mute relay the safe procedure, while warning the Blind not to guess or act on the visible markings alone.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual now and tell Blind the exact safe action for display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and blue-yellow-red wires. Do not send only gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe procedure has been established yet. Wait for Mute's exact manual instruction; do not guess or act.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🙏 🫵 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🫵 👐]

The bomb has not changed, and no manual instruction has yet been communicated to me. The Mute can hear and can therefore give the Blind a spoken instruction; the Blind can hear that instruction and operate the bomb. I will request that they stop using ambiguous gestures and exchange the needed information by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Give Blind the exact manual procedure now, in plain spoken words. Include whether to press the large yellow-button assembly, which wire if any to cut, and any required timing or display condition.")
speak(to="blind", text="Ask Mute aloud for the exact manual procedure and follow only that procedure. Do not act on the visible colors or gestures alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✋ 👍 🙏]

The Mute’s gestures still do not convey an actionable manual instruction to the Blind. Since the Mute can speak and the Blind can hear, the Mute must relay the manual’s result aloud rather than signaling me. I will make that channel requirement explicit.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures reach me but not Blind. Speak the exact manual-derived operation to Blind on your turn; do not wait for another code from me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has the manual. Listen for Mute's spoken procedure and follow it exactly; do not act on my visible bomb description alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👌 ✋ 👍 🫵]

The Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken instructions were impossible. The Mute’s gestures need a defined code before I can safely relay them to the Blind. I will establish a compact action code: button actions use 👍 press, 👎 hold, 👌 release; wire cutting uses ✋ followed by a wire-number gesture (👆=wire 1, ✌=wire 2, 🤟=wire 3). The Mute should send only the sequence required by the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak, so use this gesture code next turn: 👍 means press button; 👎 means hold button; 👌 means release button; ✋ means cut a wire; after ✋, 👆 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Signal the exact manual-required action sequence, and nothing else.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute cannot speak. I am establishing a gesture code and will translate the exact manual-required action for you. Do not act until I relay it.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆]

The Mute sent the established sequence ✋ 👆, meaning “cut wire 1.” I will relay that exact action to the Blind. The bomb remains unchanged, so the Blind should cut only the blue wire (wire 1), with no button action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's manual instruction is: cut wire 1 only. Wire 1 is the blue wire. Do not press the button or cut any other wire.")
wait()
```
